paperTitle: O-Level Basic Band — Practice 09: The Durian
provenanceNote: NOT STUDENT-FACING. Basic band. Original narrative written for the morning-quiz bank; NOT from any past exam paper. Short passage (~230 words, everyday vocabulary), 2 short-answer + 3 MCQ. Most marks reachable by choosing — typed items run a 64% blank rate in the weakest cohort.

sections.instruction: Read the story below and answer the questions that follow. [2 marks]. Write short answers.
sections.passage:
Paragraph 1
My father buys one durian every June. Only one, and always from the same stall.

Paragraph 2
The man at the stall is called Uncle Teo. He has known my father since they were boys in the same village school.

Paragraph 3
This year the durian cost sixty dollars. My mother said it was too much. My father paid anyway.

Paragraph 4
We ate it at the table with newspaper spread out. My sister would not touch it. She says it smells like gas.

Paragraph 5
My father does not eat much of it either. He takes one small piece and then watches the rest of us.

Paragraph 6
I asked him why he buys it if he hardly eats it.

Paragraph 7
He said that when he was nine, his family could not afford durian. He would stand outside the shop and smell it. He promised himself that when he had money he would buy one every year.

Paragraph 8
He has kept that promise for thirty-one years. Some years the durian was small. One year he bought it two weeks late because the price was too high. But he has never missed a June.

Paragraph 9
Next June I will pay for it. I have already told Uncle Teo. He laughed and said my father would argue about it. I think he is right, and I think I will win.
